H1.text: Pump up a bicycle tyre, then watch the little valve as the wheel turns.

H2.text: Sometimes above the hub, sometimes below. Sometimes to the right, sometimes to the left.

H3.text: Diya spotted this while Aarav was fixing his front wheel after class.

H4.text: She asked: when the valve is below the hub, is its height a minus number?

H5.text: It is. And that one idea decides the sign of every trigonometric function, in all four quadrants.

P1.text: Quick recall. Draw a circle of radius one, with its centre at the origin O. This is the unit circle.

P3.text: Turn an angle theta from the positive x axis. The arm ends at a point P on the circle.

P4.text: The x coordinate of P is cosine theta. The y coordinate is sine theta.

P5.text: So cosine tells you left or right. Sine tells you up or down. Right and up are plus. Left and down are minus.

S1.text: Now let P travel all the way round, and watch the signs.

S2.text: First quadrant, theta from zero to pi by two. P is to the right and above. Cosine is plus, sine is plus.

S3.text: Second quadrant, from pi by two to pi. P crosses to the left. Cosine turns minus, but sine stays plus.

S4.text: Third quadrant, from pi to three pi by two. P is left and below. Cosine and sine are both minus.

S5.text: Fourth quadrant, three pi by two to two pi. P is back on the right, but below. Cosine is plus, sine is minus.

S6.text: Now look at the sine graph. It stays above the axis for the first half turn, and below it for the second half.

D1.text: The other four functions are built from sine and cosine, so their signs follow.

D2.text: Step one. Tangent is sine divided by cosine.

D3.text: Step two. When you divide, same signs give plus, and opposite signs give minus.

D4.text: Step three. Sine and cosine have the same sign only in the first and third quadrants. So tangent is plus there, and minus in the other two.

D5.text: Step four. Cosecant is one over sine, so it copies the sign of sine. Secant copies cosine. Cotangent copies tangent.

K1.text: Side by side. Sixty degrees is in the first quadrant. Sine is about zero point eight seven, and cosine is plus a half.

K2.text: One hundred and twenty degrees is in the second quadrant. The sine is the same. But the cosine flips to minus a half.

K3.text: Same height, opposite sides. The quadrant gives the sign.

K4.text: Now you try. Is cosine of two hundred degrees positive or negative? Pause and decide.

K5.text: Negative! Two hundred degrees is in the third quadrant, where P is to the left of O.

M1.text: A quick way to remember: start in the first quadrant, and go anticlockwise.

M2.text: First quadrant, all six are plus. Second, only sine and cosecant. Third, only tangent and cotangent. Fourth, only cosine and secant.

M3.text: All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine. Or remember: All Students Take Coffee.

T1.text: Remember this. Going anticlockwise from the first quadrant: All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine.

Z1.text: Quick one. Sine is negative, but tangent is positive. Which quadrant is P in? Pause and think.

Z2.text: The third! Sine is minus in the third and fourth. Tangent is plus in the first and third. Only the third has both.

W2.text: Theta is in the second quadrant, and sine theta is three fifths. Find cosine and tangent.

W3.text: Step one. P is on the unit circle, so cosine squared plus sine squared is one.

W4.text: Step two. Cosine squared is sixteen over twenty five. So cosine is plus or minus four fifths.

W5.text: Step three. In the second quadrant, P is to the left of the centre. So cosine theta is minus four fifths.

W6.text: Step four. Tangent is sine over cosine. Three fifths divided by minus four fifths is minus three quarters.

W7.text: The quadrant, not the arithmetic, chose the sign.

X2.text: Many students think: in the third quadrant, everything is negative. So tangent must be negative too.

X3.text: But tangent is sine over cosine, and minus over minus is plus. At two hundred and twenty five degrees, tangent is plus one.

J1.text: Where is this asked? In PUC exams and JEE Main: one ratio and the quadrant are given, find the others.

Q1.text: Exam level now. Find the value of this expression. Pause and solve.

A2.text: Tangent is negative, and cosine is positive. That only happens in the fourth quadrant, so sine is negative.

A3.text: Tangent is minus five over twelve, so think of a five, twelve, thirteen triangle.

A4.text: So sine theta is minus five over thirteen, and cosine theta is twelve over thirteen.

A5.text: The expression becomes minus five plus twenty four, which is nineteen.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. In which quadrant are sine and cosine both negative?

Y3.text: Two. Is tangent of three hundred degrees positive or negative?

Y4.text: Three. Why does cosecant always have the same sign as sine?

N1.text: Next time: the valve can never rise higher than the wheel's radius. So how big can sine ever get? We find out in domain and range of trigonometric functions.
